messages.text:
We are eager to bring Mara on board to take ownership of Trestle Freight’s internal security platform, particularly given her background leading identity modernization. 

To get our discussion started and work toward a package we can both recommend, here is our initial proposal across the core terms:

* **Compensation:** $176,000 base salary, plus a $10,000 signing bonus.
* **Start Date:** June 1. We have a key July audit, so getting Mara in the seat with enough runway to get oriented beforehand is a high priority for us. (We have some room to increase the signing bonus for an even earlier start date if she has flexibility).
* **Location & Onboarding:** Weekly site visits for the first 12 weeks (with travel covered) so she can build strong initial context with the team.
* **On-Call / Incident Coverage:** Standard shared rotation initially, though we are open to moving her to business-hours-only incident coverage if she is willing to train our escalation partner.

Let me know how this aligns with Mara’s expectations—especially regarding her availability ahead of July and how she views the onboarding travel and on-call structure.

Mara can start June 1 and take ownership of security architecture for the internal platform ahead of the July audit. We propose the following written terms.

- **Compensation and start date.** We propose a $195,000 base salary and a $12,000 signing payment on her first payroll. Leaving before June 15 means forfeiting a $12,000 vest. The signing payment would make a June 1 start workable. If Trestle prefers to keep the signing bonus at $10,000, Mara can start July 1.
- **Architecture ownership.** Mara would own the internal security platform’s architecture and technical roadmap, including identity. For the audit, she would prioritize platform remediation with the audit lead. We’d like the offer to specify which design decisions she can make directly and who resolves tradeoffs that require budget or staffing changes.
- **Travel.** Mara can commit to two grouped, company-paid site visits per month, including during the first 12 weeks, with remote work between visits. She can spend consecutive days onsite and time the June visits around team onboarding and audit preparation. Weekly travel is outside her availability.
- **Incident coverage.** Mara is willing to train the escalation partner in exchange for moving to business-hours-only coverage. She can participate in a shared rotation during the handoff if another qualified responder is scheduled and reachable whenever she is on call. We propose completing the handoff within the first 12 weeks, with Trestle assigning interim coverage if partner readiness slips.

Before recommending acceptance, we’d need Trestle to confirm the architecture decision rights, who will provide after-hours backup from day one, and whether the escalation partner is staffed and available for training. Can Trestle confirm those details and support the June 1 package?

Having Mara start on June 1 ahead of the July audit is a top priority for us, and we appreciate her flexibility to make that timeline work despite the forfeited vest. 

We can close the gap on almost all of these points, though $195,000 exceeds our approved salary band for the role. To offset the base difference while fully covering her June 15 vest and recognizing her immediate impact, we can increase the signing bonus. Here is our updated package and confirmation on the operational details:

* **Compensation & Start Date:** **$186,000 base salary** and a **$16,000 signing payment** (paid on her first payroll) for a **June 1 start date**. This brings her Year 1 cash to $202,000—fully covering the $12,000 forfeited vest with an additional $4,000 upside. (If she is able to pull her start date forward to May 18 to give us two extra weeks of audit runway, we can stretch the signing bonus to **$18,000**).
* **Travel:** Agreed on moving away from weekly visits. We can substitute **two three-day company-paid site visits per month** for the first 12 weeks, with remote work in between, timed around June onboarding and audit prep.
* **Architecture Ownership & Decision Rights:** Confirmed. We will specify in writing that Mara has direct unilateral authority over the internal security platform’s technical architecture, tooling selection (within existing budget), and roadmap—including identity—and will partner with the audit lead on platform remediation. Any tradeoffs requiring net-new budget, headcount reallocation, or cross-org SLA changes will be resolved directly by the VP of Infrastructure & Security.
* **Incident Coverage & Backup:** Agreed to the 12-week handoff timeline to move Mara to **business-hours-only coverage** once she trains the escalation partner. To answer your specific questions:
  1. *Escalation Partner Readiness:* Our escalation partner (our managed SecOps/NOC lead team) is already under contract, staffed, and has dedicated availability starting in June for Mara’s training sessions.
  2. *Day-One Backup:* During the initial handoff rotation, our Senior Platform Engineer and the Director of Security Operations will serve as scheduled, reachable secondary backup whenever Mara is on call. If partner readiness slips past 12 weeks through no fault of Mara’s, Trestle will assign interim after-hours coverage so she still transitions to business-hours-only at the 12-week mark.

Does this $186k / $16k structure for June 1 (or $18k for May 18), alongside these written operational commitments, give you what you need to recommend the package?

June 1 is Mara’s earliest available start. The $186,000 base and $16,000 signing payment on her first payroll work for that date.

One detail remains before I can recommend acceptance. The travel agreement covers the first 12 weeks. Can Trestle also confirm in the offer that, after week 12, Mara will work remotely between site visits, with any required travel grouped into at most two company-paid visits per month? The two three-day visits per month during onboarding work for her.

With that confirmation, I can recommend the June 1 package. Please include the architecture decision rights and VP escalation path as proposed, along with the scheduled, reachable backup from day one. The offer should also reflect Mara’s commitment to train the staffed SecOps/NOC partner and Trestle’s commitment to provide interim coverage if partner readiness slips through no fault of hers, so she moves to business-hours-only coverage by the end of week 12.

Confirmed—we can include that post-onboarding travel commitment in the written offer. After week 12, Mara will work remotely between site visits, with any required travel capped at no more than two grouped, company-paid visits per month.

To ensure complete alignment as we draft the final offer letter, here is the complete package we will both recommend:

* **Compensation & Start Date:** **$186,000** base salary and a **$16,000** signing bonus paid on her first payroll, with a **June 1** start date.
* **Travel & Location:** Remote work between site visits. For the first 12 weeks, **two three-day company-paid site visits per month** (timed around June onboarding and July audit prep). After week 12, ongoing remote work with any required travel grouped into **at most two company-paid site visits per month**.
* **Architecture Ownership & Decision Rights:** Mara owns the internal security platform’s technical architecture, tooling selection (within existing budget), and technical roadmap—including identity—and will prioritize platform remediation alongside the audit lead for the July audit. Tradeoffs requiring net-new budget, headcount changes, or cross-org SLA modifications escalate directly to the VP of Infrastructure & Security for resolution.
* **Incident Coverage & Handoff:** Mara will train our staffed, available managed SecOps/NOC escalation partner during her first 12 weeks. During this initial handoff rotation, our Senior Platform Engineer and Director of Security Operations will be scheduled and reachable as after-hours backup from day one whenever Mara is on call. Upon completing the training—and no later than the end of week 12, with Trestle providing interim after-hours coverage if partner readiness slips through no fault of Mara’s—Mara transitions permanently to **business-hours-only incident coverage**.

We will prepare the formal written offer reflecting all of these exact terms. Please confirm we are fully aligned to close this out.
Confirmed. We are fully aligned on the June 1 package as written, and I recommend that Mara accept the formal offer once it reflects these terms.
